title: Prefix-aware metric enrichment and stateless OTLP filter for cardinality-safe inference KPIs
creator: Maya Li
description: Implement a lightweight, prefix-aware enrichment layer placed between our serving runtime sidecar and the OTLP collector that attaches deterministic, low-cardinality attributes for inference requests (request_bucket, model_family, serving_mode) and rewrites high-cardinality values into stable buckets. The enrichment runs as a stateless filter to avoid PII leakage and to enable downstream Prometheus remote-write and KPI dashboards without exploding label cardinality. Deliverables: OTLP filter implementation, Prometheus remote-write adapter rules, updated ingestion docs, and dashboard panels for request_bucket heatmaps and model_family latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: OTLP enrichment filter deployed as a canary in dev and staging clusters
Metric labels normalized: original_high_cardinality values replaced with deterministic bucket labels and original omitted from Prometheus exports
End-to-end pipeline verified using synthetic traffic: ingestion throughput within 10% of baseline and no increase in memory beyond 5% on collector replicas
Updated dashboards display request_bucket and model_family SLOs with correct aggregation and no cardinality spikes
Code reviewed and merged; migration KB published and rollback documented

comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Li: Created ticket. Initial design doc linked below. Goal: reduce cardinality wins while preserving actionable KPIs for latency and error attribution.

2025-02-19 Ravi Patel: POC completed for enrichment filter. Implementation uses deterministic hashing mod N to create request_bucket. Observed 0.8% additional CPU on a collector replica under 10k rps synthetic workload.

2025-02-21 SRE (Nina Gomez): Concern about losing request-level troubleshooting signals. Proposed compromise: keep original request_id in trace spans (not in metrics) and emit a debug metric with original id only under 1% sampling for debugging windows.

2025-03-03 Code reviewer (Elena Rossi): Left review comments on deterministic hash salt rotation and ensuring roll-forward compatibility in Prometheus rules. Request adding unit tests that assert stable bucket mapping across restarts.

notes: Trade-offs: we deliberately avoid storing original high-cardinality IDs in metrics to keep Prometheus storage costs predictable. The team decided to preserve original IDs in traces only and to provide deterministic sampling for temporally-limited debug sessions. We will revisit bucket width (N) after two weeks of canary telemetry. Proposed default N=256 for request_bucket which balances resolution and cardinality.
